items.claim: The row states an arithmetically false numbering-space identity for the offset zone and leaves its front seam - the book's crosswalk seam - uncited, while the tier-1 gender marker its own signal key rests on runs unbroken across that cut.
items.evidence: VERIFIED FIRST: both quoted runs re-collate at BYTE tier against their cited MT refs, and both duals land on the right content - web:Song.7.1 = oshb:Song.7.2 does carry מַה יָּפ֧וּ פְעָמַ֛יִךְ בַּנְּעָלִ֖ים and web:Song.7.5 = oshb:Song.7.6 does carry מֶ֖לֶךְ אָס֥וּר בָּרְהָטִֽים; the suffixed body-part chain genuinely does begin at MT 7:2 (MT 7:1 has no suffixed body-part noun). DEFECT 1 (crosswalk prose): the parenthetical 'WEB ch 7 = MT 7:2-7:6' is false - WEB ch 7 (13 verses) = MT 7:2-7:14; MT 7:2-7:6 is only this row's own span (= WEB 7:1-7:5). A false numbering-space identity written inside the zone where dual discipline binds hardest. DEFECT 2 (front seam): the front neighbour web:Song.6.13 = oshb:Song.7.1 appears in no evidence ref and in no prose, yet its bytes carry the 2fs imperative שׁ֤וּבִי (four times in that verse) and the 2fs suffix וְנֶחֱזֶה בָּ֑ךְ (byte tier) - so the 2fs address marker is CONTINUOUS across the front cut and only the body-part sub-class starts at MT 7:2; the praise-exclamation construction also straddles that cut, מַֽה תֶּחֱזוּ֙ at MT 7:1 answered by מַה יָּפ֧וּ at MT 7:2 (skeleton-tier sweep of that construction: 3 verses - MT 4:10, MT 7:2 = WEB 7:1, MT 7:7 = WEB 7:6). Undisclosed cross-seam continuity. DEFECT 3 (gloss): the closure gloss reads 'the king' for the anarthrous מֶ֖לֶךְ at MT 7:6 = WEB 7:5, which is the one article-less member of the 5-verse melek-lexeme set; the definiteness is the WEB rendering, not the bytes. Finally, the boundary warrant in both the rationale and the rejected alternative is the mechanically derived run, which is a staging signal and not row evidence. AUDIT NOTE (tier-4, non-evidential, offered only as an audit against heading-leaning): this uncited front seam falls exactly at a WEB [SPEAKER] apparatus site before web:Song.7.1.

items.claim: The single-verse cut is carried by a voice-shift signal key, but the bytes show no shift at all - same speaker, same 2fs addressee across MT 7:6-7:8 - and the vocative construal that supplies the only other warrant is undecidable on the staged evidence.
items.evidence: VERIFIED FIRST: the quoted run re-collates at BYTE tier at oshb:Song.7.7, the dual web:Song.7.6 = oshb:Song.7.7 lands on the right content, and the ahavah-noun digit (10 verses) names the right object, correctly split from the she-ahavah relative-verb formula. DEFECT 1 (no voice shift in the bytes): MT 7:7 addresses one second-person addressee with the perfect forms מַה יָּפִית֙ וּמַה נָּעַ֔מְתְּ, whose attested endings carry no final qamats - they are not the 2ms counterparts - and the flanking verses fix that addressee as feminine on byte-attested 2fs suffixes, MT 7:6 רֹאשֵׁ֤ךְ עָלַ֨יִךְ֙ and MT 7:8 זֹ֤את קֽוֹמָתֵךְ֙, with both witnesses reading a continuous address. No speaker change, no addressee change, no address-vocabulary vocative, no refrain anchor: the voice_shift signal key is unsupported by the row's own verse, and cutting a sustained single-voice run at a point carrying no tier-1 voice-shift marker is precisely what the granularity rule forbids. DEFECT 2 (construal asserted, not held): the vocative reading of אַהֲבָ֖ה בַּתַּֽעֲנוּגִֽים is decided, not disclosed - the noun is anarthrous and morphologically unmarked for vocative, no morphology layer is staged, and the rival construal (love itself as the exclamation's subject) stands equally on these bytes; the vocative follows the WEB rendering, so the driver is translation-dependent. DEFECT 3 (undisclosed cross-seam construction): the same praise-exclamation shape opens the preceding row's first verse, מַה יָּפ֧וּ at MT 7:2 = WEB 7:1, and this verse, מַה יָּפִית֙ at MT 7:7 = WEB 7:6 (skeleton-tier sweep: 3 verses, MT 4:10 / 7:2 / 7:7) - a byte-true device straddling the row's own front seam, arguing continuity against the isolation and nowhere disclosed. The stated driver that remains, absence of a suffixed body-part noun, is a form sub-class and not a tier-1 marker.

items.claim: The row's own last verse carries her address-word for him, undisclosed, contradicting the row's single-voice attribution and binding that verse forward into the mutual-belonging refrain across the row's back seam.
items.evidence: VERIFIED FIRST: both quoted runs re-collate at BYTE tier at oshb:Song.7.8 and oshb:Song.7.10, and both duals land on the right content. DEFECT 1 (tier-1 marker of the OTHER voice inside the span, undisclosed): oshb:Song.7.10 = web:Song.7.9 - the row's own final verse - reads הוֹלֵ֥ךְ לְדוֹדִ֖י לְמֵישָׁרִ֑ים (byte tier), carrying the dodi address-word, which is her word for him and one of the two tier-1 address vocabularies; the row quotes only that verse's closing three words דּוֹבֵ֖ב שִׂפְתֵ֥י יְשֵׁנִֽים and never mentions it. It is visible in both witnesses - WEB renders the clause “for my beloved” at web:Song.7.9. A row typed as his praise poem of her, with a single sustained voice, cannot leave her address-word standing unremarked inside its own final verse. DEFECT 2 (undisclosed cross-seam device): that same token repeats immediately across the back seam at oshb:Song.7.11 = web:Song.7.10, אֲנִ֣י לְדוֹדִ֔י (byte tier), and the dod-family chain then runs unbroken through MT 7:12 לְכָ֤ה דוֹדִי֙, the defective form at MT 7:13, and MT 7:14 - five consecutive MT verses, 7:10-7:14 = WEB 7:9-7:13 (skeleton-tier sweep of the dod family over that run). A byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed, and here it also relocates the plausible voice turn to inside MT 7:10 rather than at the row's chosen seam. DEFECT 3: the boundary warrant offered in the rationale and in the rejected alternative is the mechanically derived run, a staging signal that is not row evidence. AUDIT NOTE (tier-4, non-evidential): the chosen back seam coincides exactly with a WEB [SPEAKER] apparatus site before web:Song.7.10 - the one place where the row's own Hebrew evidence in fact runs the other way.

items.claim: Every claim the row makes verifies byte-for-byte, but its forward seam is argued by nothing except a tier-3 mark while the dod-family chain and her continuing first-person voice run straight through both of its edges undisclosed.
items.evidence: VERIFIED FIRST (an unusually clean set): אֲנִ֣י לְדוֹדִ֔י וְעָלַ֖י תְּשׁוּקָתֽוֹ re-collates at BYTE tier at oshb:Song.7.11; the dual web:Song.7.10 = oshb:Song.7.11 is arithmetically right AND lands on the right content, which is the offset-zone trap this cluster was flagged for; this is genuinely the third mutual-belonging site, quoted at its own attested wording and not harmonized with דּוֹדִ֥י לִי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י ל֔וֹ at MT 2:16 or the order-flipped אֲנִ֤י לְדוֹדִי֙ וְדוֹדִ֣י לִ֔י at MT 6:3, so the 3-site object is correctly named; and the setumah is in the inventory at MT 7:11 under the claimed type, MT-keyed, with single-witness disclosed and corroborative framing. DEFECT 1 (driverless forward seam): the forward seam oshb:Song.7.11 | oshb:Song.7.12 (= web:Song.7.10 | web:Song.7.11) is supported by that mark and by nothing else - the parashah layer is tier-3 weak corroboration in the Writings and never a boundary driver, and the row's rejected alternative addresses only the backward cut. Across that seam MT 7:12 opens לְכָ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ (byte tier), the same dodi vocative, in the same first-person voice, so no tier-1 marker sits at the forward cut. DEFECT 2 (undisclosed cross-seam chain): the dod family runs MT 7:10, 7:11, 7:12, 7:13 (defective spelling) and 7:14 - five consecutive MT verses = WEB 7:9-7:13, skeleton tier - straddling BOTH of this one-verse row's seams with no disclosure; in particular the immediately preceding verse already reads לְדוֹדִ֖י, which undercuts the rejected alternative's 'distinct genre' warrant. DEFECT 3: that backward warrant leans on the mechanically derived run, a staging signal rather than row evidence. Under the hybrid granularity ruling a refrain verse CLOSES a unit; isolating it instead requires an argued forward driver, which is absent.

items.claim: The row names a Hebrew form that is not in its span - MT 7:13 reads the 1cs defective dodai, not a 2ms 'dodekha' - and its mandrake and cohortative labels are likewise off the bytes.
items.evidence: VERIFIED FIRST: both quoted runs re-collate at BYTE tier at oshb:Song.7.12 and oshb:Song.7.14; the duals land on the right content; the front-seam citation oshb:Song.7.11 = web:Song.7.10 is arithmetically right and the setumah is in the inventory there under the claimed type with single-witness disclosure; and the row is right to hold the defective spelling and the mandrakes apart from the dodi-exact count. DEFECT 1 (byte-false form, in the row that owns the token): the attested defective token at oshb:Song.7.13 = web:Song.7.12 is אֶת דֹּדַ֖י לָֽךְ - the consonants carry NO second-person suffix at all, and both witnesses read it as the speaker's own possessive - WEB “There I will give you my love” at web:Song.7.12 - against WEB “your love” at the second-person members web:Song.1.2 and web:Song.4.10. The row calls it 'the defective-spelling dodekha token', a second-person masculine form that is not in these bytes; the skeleton sweep for the defective spelling returns 4 verses (MT 1:2, 1:4, 4:10, 7:13 = WEB 1:2, 1:4, 4:10, 7:12), of which MT 7:13 is the member whose suffix runs the other way. Wrong form and wrong direction of address, in the row that owns the token and argues from who is addressing whom. DEFECT 2 (unscoped universal): הַֽדּוּדָאִ֣ים at oshb:Song.7.14 = web:Song.7.13 is called a 'hapax' with no scope and no digit; the staged sweep supports only the book-scoped digit, 1 verse in this book, which is what the universal-claim discipline requires it to say. DEFECT 3 (form label off the bytes): 'one sustained 1cs voice' and 'her single cohortative address' mis-state the run - the cohortatives in the span are first-person PLURAL, נֵצֵ֣א, נָלִ֖ינָה, נַשְׁכִּ֨ימָה֙ and נִרְאֶ֞ה, all nun-prefixed and rendered as plurals by both witnesses; the genuinely 1cs forms are אֶתֵּ֥ן and צָפַ֥נְתִּי. The signal key naming a 1cs cohortative inherits the error. Also noted: the back seam oshb:Song.7.14 | oshb:Song.8.1 (= web:Song.7.13 | web:Song.8.1) carries no cited ref and no argument on either side of the pair.

items.claim: The opening cut splits a continuous first-person-to-2ms address with no tier-1 voice-shift marker and no cited front-seam ref at all, and the closing quote's gloss drops half of what the quote contains.
items.evidence: VERIFIED FIRST: both quoted runs re-collate at BYTE tier at oshb:Song.8.1 and oshb:Song.8.3, and the row's one properly quoted gender claim is correct - מִ֤י יִתֶּנְךָ֙ does carry the 2ms suffix in the bytes. DEFECT 1 (cut without a tier-1 marker, seam uncited): the front seam web:Song.7.13 = oshb:Song.7.14 | web:Song.8.1 is cited nowhere in the evidence refs and argued only as a 'fresh movement'. Across it neither speaker nor addressee changes: MT 7:14 closes דּוֹדִ֖י צָפַ֥נְתִּי לָֽךְ - her first-person verb under the dodi vocative of that same verse, WEB “which I have stored up for you, my beloved” at web:Song.7.13 - and MT 8:1 continues אֶֽמְצָאֲךָ֤ and אֶשָׁ֣קְךָ֔, first-person verbs carrying 2ms object suffixes, both witnesses concurring. A wish particle is not in the tier-1 marker set (gendered forms, vocatives, attested formula anchors) and marks no shift here, so a maximal single-voice run is being cut with no qualifying driver, and the one seam that would have to bear the argument is undisclosed. DEFECT 2 (quote/gloss parity): the run quoted at oshb:Song.8.3 is שְׂמֹאלוֹ֙ תַּ֣חַת רֹאשִׁ֔י וִֽימִינ֖וֹ, which ends on the 'and his right hand' word that the gloss 'his left hand under my head' does not render, and the quote is cut off before the verb תְּחַבְּקֵֽנִי that governs it - the quote and its gloss do not cover the same text. DEFECT 3 (untiered recurrence claim): the 8:3 echo is asserted with no tier label and is NOT byte-identical to its earlier counterpart - MT 2:6 reads תַּ֣חַת לְרֹאשִׁ֔י against MT 8:3 תַּ֣חַת רֹאשִׁ֔י, the lamed present in the earlier verse and absent here; under the tier-disclosure standard this is a skeleton-adjacent echo and has to say so.

items.claim: The row's adjuration objects all verify, but the contrast shape it names for MT 5:8 is not the attested one, and the verse whose shape it contrasts is argued in prose without being carried in the evidence refs.
items.evidence: VERIFIED FIRST (most of this row is right): both quoted runs re-collate at BYTE tier at oshb:Song.8.4; the mah-ta'iru shape claim holds - MT 8:4 reads מַה תָּעִ֧ירוּ וּֽמַה תְּעֹֽרְר֛וּ and carries no gazelle-and-doe pairing, against the full form at MT 2:7 = MT 3:5 which reads בִּצְבָא֔וֹת א֖וֹ בְּאַיְל֣וֹת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה; MT 8:4 is genuinely the fourth of exactly four oath sites; the daughters-vocative בְּנ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם is the address form rather than the from-phrase; the quoted-back oath at MT 5:9 is correctly excluded from the site count and correctly mirrored in the refs; the setumah is in the inventory at MT 8:4 under the claimed type, single-witness disclosed; and MT 8:4 is outside the offset zone, so the bare web: refs are legitimate there. DEFECT 1 (byte-false shape name): 'the mah-timtze'u shape' is not attested anywhere. MT 5:8 reads אִֽם תִּמְצְאוּ֙ - the conditional particle with that verb - and its interrogative attaches to a different verb, מַה תַּגִּ֣ידוּ. The row blends the two particles of the 5:8 variant into a single invented name in the very note that claims formula-variation discipline; the attested contrast is the im-timtze'u / mah-tagidu shape. DEFECT 2 (unmirrored ref): MT 5:8 = web:Song.5.8 is the verse whose shape is being contrasted and it appears in no evidence ref, while its neighbour 5:9 does. DEFECT 3 (register): 'held earlier in this part' is a positional/part reference in row prose, where cross-row references are supposed to be verse-anchored.
